reader.requirement: At --std 85, after a successful CLOSE of a relative file (any access mode: sequential, random, dynamic; CLOSE and CLOSE WITH LOCK) the file is no longer in an open mode (every later READ/WRITE/REWRITE/DELETE is refused with the not-open logic status 47/48/49, a second CLOSE is 42, and a new OPEN is accepted rather than refused 41) and the connector is no longer associated with the physical file (another file connector on the same file may then open it). The witness exercises only a SEQUENTIAL-organization file; the relative organization, all three access modes, the dissociation and the after-failed-OPEN CLOSE are not exercised by it.

edition-consulted.switches: DialectBehavior.CloseWithLockLocksFileConnector: at 85 WITH LOCK locks the PHYSICAL FILE (ClosedWithLock on the physical-file state), from 2002 the connector; this is GR2 symbol B, not GR6, and the open-mode removal and SharedClose dissociation run before it identically

reader.edition-search: grep -n 'Edition|CobolVersion|Dialect' over src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime/IO/*.cs and read FileRegistry.CloseCell/CloseByFormat/SharedClose, FileConnector.Close and SequentialIoEmitter.EmitClose: the plain CLOSE path (Table14 cell lookup, SharedClose's Open.Remove, _openMode=false, ModeKnown=false) consults no edition; only CloseWithLock's lock target does.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no (for GR6: the open-mode removal and dissociation are one code path at every edition; only what WITH LOCK locks differs, which is GR2 B)
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness is a sequential-organization file; the relative organization in random, dynamic and sequential access, dissociation from the connector (a second SELECT of the same file opening after the CLOSE), and CLOSE after a failed OPEN are exercised only by probe p1close

probes.expected: after each successful CLOSE the file is not in an open mode: READ 47, WRITE 48, REWRITE/DELETE 49 (§1985:VIII.1.3.4 statuses), second CLOSE 42, re-OPEN succeeds 00 (not 41); a second connector (R2, dynamic) on the same physical file opens I-O 00 after R's CLOSE; same for random, dynamic and sequential access
a failed OPEN (35, non-optional absent) leaves the file not open, so CLOSE is 42; CLOSE WITH LOCK removes the file from the open mode and a re-OPEN is 38 (§1985:VIII.1.3.4 status 38)

reader.notes: The plain CLOSE path is edition-free: FileRegistry.CloseCell runs SharedClose (deregisters the connector from the physical file) then FileConnector.Close (clears _openMode and ModeKnown). Every verb after the CLOSE took its not-open status, re-OPEN succeeded, and a second SELECT on the same file opened after the CLOSE, for all three relative access modes.
